network.title: Server network check

exposure.natOrProxy: May be behind NAT or a proxy

network.ports: Allow these incoming ports in your provider’s firewall or NAT:

issue.endpointResolution: The public VPN address doesn’t resolve from this device. Correct it before installing.
issue.natOrProxy: The public VPN address isn’t on a server interface, so a provider NAT mapping or proxy may be in between. Forward the listed ports to this server with the same port numbers: working SSH access doesn’t mean the VPN is reachable.
issue.privateEndpoint: The VPN address is private or local, so it works only from networks that can reach it. Set a public VPN address for access from the Internet.
issue.ipv6Only: This server has no IPv4. Devices can connect only from networks with IPv6, or through a CDN in HTTPS CDN mode. IPv4-only websites fail unless you set a NAT64 prefix, and that NAT64 gateway’s operator then sees which IPv4 addresses people visit. The server’s DNS must use DNS-over-TLS or DNS-over-HTTPS with IPv6 resolver addresses.
issue.tunnelAddressConflict: {{interface}} already uses {{address}}, inside SirinVPN’s 10.77.0.0/24 network. Move that network before installing.
issue.privateServicePort: Port {{port}} is already in use on an address SirinVPN needs for a private service. Move that service before installing.
issue.sshPortConflict: TCP port {{port}} is used by SSH. Choose a different TCP or TLS port.
issue.portInUse: {{protocol}} port {{port}} is already used by another service. Choose a free port or move that service.
issue.tunnelRouteConflict: The route {{route}} on {{interface}} overlaps SirinVPN’s 10.77.0.0/24 network. Check that network before installing.
issue.reservedInterface: A network interface named sirinvpn0 already exists, but no SirinVPN server is installed. Find out what created it before installing.
issue.existingVpn: Another VPN interface is already on this server. Its routes and firewall rules are kept; check that it works alongside SirinVPN.
issue.existingFirewall: Other firewall rules are active. SirinVPN keeps them, but they may also need to allow the listed ports and the tunnel network.
issue.firewallDropPolicy: A firewall on this server drops traffic by default. If the ports are open at the provider but VPN traffic is still blocked, allow it in that firewall.
issue.firewallService: A firewall service is active on this server. SirinVPN keeps its configuration; check that it allows the listed ports and VPN traffic.
issue.other: The server check found something to review.

transport.alternateHostsPlaceholder: Up to three hostnames or IP addresses
transport.alternateNote: Each address must reach this server on the same ports.
transport.portsNote: Open these ports in your provider’s firewall. Ports 53, 5053 and 8443 are reserved.
transport.portsInfo: TCP and TLS fallback share one port, and QUIC (HTTP/3) uses the same port number over UDP. If you change it, the old port stays open so devices can receive the new one; keep it allowed in your firewall.
transport.quicNote: QUIC uses the TCP, TLS and QUIC port number over UDP, so Obfuscated UDP needs another port. Allow both UDP ports in your provider’s firewall.
transport.httpsNote: Use a hostname you control. Leave both paths empty to use a generated, pinned certificate.
transport.httpsInfo: The server keeps its own copy of your certificate. After renewing it, import it here so devices get the new pin. Some networks may still block HTTPS mode.
transport.cdnPortNote: Cloudflare proxies HTTPS only on ports 443, 2053, 2083, 2087 and 2096. Check that your CDN proxies this TCP and TLS port.
transport.cdnNote: For when this VPS address is blocked. In your CDN, proxy the hostname to this VPS with WebSockets on and full, not strict, TLS. The CDN sees device addresses, timing and traffic volume, never what goes through the tunnel.
transport.existingNote: Before changing ports or certificates, cancel waiting join codes and finish key rotations.
transport.invalid: Check the ports, hostname, path and certificate paths.

missing.port: Enter an SSH port from 1 to 65535.
